title: Large personal Amiga, Spectrum, ST and CPC tooling discovery
summary: Personally screen 119 candidate URLs, inspect 30 repository roots, add 29 projects and record one empty-repository exclusion.
notes: All research and publication performed by the root assistant without a research worker, PR or new branch. Five fresh searches focused on DOS extraction, Spectrum disassembly, Amiga tools, GFA software and CPC engines. Thirty selected roots received primary-source inspection; one was confirmed empty, while tokenized GFA archives are explicitly qualified as documentation/artifact review rather than decoded source. Meaningful native code, parsers, historical utilities and educational engines are separated from completeness, cycle-accuracy and generated-C claims. Runtime LLM use and neural-network subject matter do not automatically set development-AI metadata. No upstream code, executable, ROM, disk, device command or network service was run; no independently verified build/runtime claim is made. Legacy-encoded LargeCli.asm is linked at its immutable revision but omitted from inline proofs because connector-decoded bytes did not match its Git blob.

sources.reason: Parses Dreamweb room headers, graphics segments, object records, palettes, sounds and text into extracted resources. Inspected concrete room parser rather than relying on the asset-heavy tree.
Decodes MicroProse PIC/PAL graphics, sprite sheets and FONTS.CV, with atlas and JSON-index output. Inspected variable-width LZW implementation and framing.
GXL resource extraction and multiple image/audio converters coexist with executable-analysis and generated-C experiments. Inspected real archive parsing and C generation.
Substantial annotated disassembly names objects, ball counts, drawing buffers, tables and game routines, with separated graphics and level data.
Compact native Z80 disassembler with internal stack, IX/IY undocumented-register decoding and relocation support.
Integrated Z80 assembler, disassembler, real-time debugger and Spectrum emulator, with stepping and breakpoint support. Inspected opcode tables and implementation tree.
Shared Z80 decoder feeds interpreter/disassembler; explicit machine-cycle primitives expose per-T-state bus traces. Bevy frontend and headless testing paths exist.
Native CD Changer and SD Transfer utilities issue toolbox SCSI commands to BlueSCSI V2/ZuluSCSI. Reviewed device capability setup and command dispatch.
ADFLib-based ADF creation, copying, extraction, listing, deletion and bootblock utilities. Inspected extraction traversal.
Maintained console, diff, file-manager, editor, terminal and benchmark family. Concrete patience-diff implementation uses unique-line anchors and bounded recursion.
Historical utility enlarges the boot CLI by 56 vertical pixels using Intuition window sizing. Actual small assembly implementation inspected.
GUI and service library patch known Kickstart revisions or locate a 68k instruction pattern to change startup video behavior.
Batch C/assembly build scripts, Docker toolchain recipe and PNG conversion helper preserve an earlier Amiga development workflow.
Documents original integer-to-string disassembly and replacement logic for AmigaStart’s Fast RAM display overflow, with a pattern-checked patcher.
Reusable make definitions and native device/worker examples support vbcc, amiga-gcc, AROS GCC and SAS/C through vamos.
Renoise extension parses IFF VHDR/BODY chunks, loop points and signed 8-bit mono samples, with a raw PCM path.
MUI-based hardware/system viewer uses Identify.library plus optional graphics/PCI providers and native assembly benchmarks.
Doom sound forwarding library and CAMD/MUS playback tools provide native MIDI integration. Reviewed library exports and build targets.
Author archive contains Henon/Kaneko-style map applications, movie playback/save options and original tokenized GFA files with compiled programs.
Original sprite editor supports masks/automatic masking, drawing primitives, bitmap copy/paste and ICN export. Readable GFA listing and GEM resources are present.
Author reconstructed a Mandelbrot plotting program from surviving printed listings, with a readable GFA listing and historical plots/scans.
Recovered early-1990s BBS archive includes tokenized GFA sources, distribution material and documented command functions for mail, files and administration.
Syntax grammar, snippets, completion, hover documentation and procedure/symbol navigation for GFA listings. Inspected actual extension provider registrations.
Preserves 1993 NNCK trainer, tutorial, control/network examples and surviving GFA utility/client listings. Reviewed GFAUTILS routines and provenance.
Modular Z80, AY, CRTC/ASIC, FDC and memory components with WebGPU/Canvas and WebAudio adapters. Inspected bus interface and CPU implementation.
Compact teaching implementation has editable tile map, player collision/movement and falling-rock updates rather than only a title-screen mockup.
Real CPC BASIC clients render a server-driven text adventure with history, inventory-oriented commands, mode selection and AY effects. Modern host supplies LLM narrative.
Small firmware-independent sound-effect engine drives PSG channel A from nine-byte note records with noise/envelope/vibrato flags.
Mode-1 adaptation of the MPAGD CPC engine includes 256×192 display layout, relocated tables, sprite drawing and game runtime source.

Repository search describes an Atari project, but GitHub tree retrieval reports an empty repository (HTTP 409). No implementation is available to inspect at this review; exclude the empty listing, not the idea of a future game.
